body:
Product pages and reviews use a great deal of shorthand, and it can feel like a different language when you first start shopping. This glossary groups the terms you will meet most often into device terms, electrical terms, style terms, liquid terms, experience terms and shopping terms, with a plain explanation of each and links to our fuller guides. It is written for adults aged 21 and over, and it describes how products work without making any health claims. Nicotine is addictive.

## How to use this glossary
Skim the sections that match what you are shopping for, and come back when a term on a product page is unfamiliar. Terms are grouped by topic so that related ideas sit together. Where a term has a full guide, we link to it.

## Device terms
- **Disposable:** a pre-filled, ready-to-use device that is replaced when finished. See [how to choose one](/blog/how-to-choose-a-disposable-vape/).
- **Pod:** a compact, replaceable liquid cartridge that clicks into a battery.
- **Pod system:** a device that uses pods, usually small and simple.
- **Mod:** a battery unit, often with adjustable power. Short for modification, from the days when users modified devices.
- **Box mod:** a mod in a rectangular body, often with removable batteries.
- **Tank:** a refillable container with a coil that screws onto a mod.
- **Atomizer:** the part that heats and vaporizes liquid, often used to mean the coil and its housing.
- **Starter kit:** a bundle that includes a device and what you need to start.
- **Open system:** a device that you refill yourself.
- **Closed system:** a device with pre-filled, sealed pods or cartridges.

## Electrical terms
- **mAh:** battery capacity, in milliamp hours. See [mAh, puffs and battery life](/blog/mah-puffs-and-battery-life-how-they-relate/).
- **Ohm (Ω):** coil resistance. Lower resistance draws more current.
- **Watt (W):** power delivered to the coil.
- **Volt (V):** electrical pressure.
- **Amp (A):** current. A battery's amp rating shows how much current it can supply.
- **USB-C:** a common charging connector.
- **Pass-through:** the ability to use a device while it charges.

See [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/) for how they relate.

## Coil terms
- **Mesh coil:** a coil made from a thin metal sheet that lines the wick. See [what is a mesh coil](/blog/what-is-a-mesh-coil/).
- **Wire coil:** a coil made from wound wire.
- **Dual coil:** a design with two coils for more vapor.
- **Priming:** soaking a new coil with liquid before use. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/).
- **Wicking:** the way liquid travels through the cotton to the coil.

## Style terms
- **MTL:** mouth-to-lung inhale, a tight draw into the mouth before inhaling.
- **DTL / sub-ohm:** direct-to-lung inhale with a low-resistance coil, usually with open airflow. See [the difference](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/).
- **Auto-draw:** a device that fires when you inhale.
- **Button-fire:** a device that fires when you press a button.
- **Boost mode:** a setting that increases power for a stronger draw.

## Liquid terms
- **E-liquid or vape juice:** the liquid that becomes vapor.
- **PG / VG:** propylene glycol and vegetable glycerin, the liquid base. See [PG and VG](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).
- **Nic salts:** a smoother type of nicotine for low-power devices. See [nicotine salts vs freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/).
- **Freebase:** the traditional form of nicotine.
- **Shortfill:** a bottle with spare room for nicotine shots.
- **Nic shot:** a bottle of concentrated nicotine for mixing.
- **Steeping:** letting liquid rest so flavors blend. See [what is steeping](/blog/what-is-steeping-and-does-it-matter/).
- **Strength:** the nicotine concentration, in mg/mL or percent. See the [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/).

## Experience terms
- **Throat hit:** the sensation of vapor on the throat. See [throat hit explained](/blog/throat-hit-explained/).
- **Ghosting:** a lingering flavor from a previous liquid.
- **Dry hit:** a harsh, burnt draw from a dry wick. See [dry hits explained](/blog/dry-hits-explained/).
- **Spitback:** hot droplets that reach your mouth.
- **Gurgling:** a bubbling sound caused by excess liquid.
- **Cloud chasing:** vaping for the largest vapor volume. See [cloud chasing vs flavor chasing](/blog/cloud-chasing-vs-flavor-chasing/).
- **Flavor chasing:** vaping for the fullest flavor.

## Shopping terms
- **Puffs:** the estimated number of draws a disposable provides; see [puff counts explained](/blog/puff-count-explained/).
- **Bundle:** a pack of several items sold together.
- **Pack size:** how many units come in a listing, such as single or 5-pack.
- **SKU:** a product's unique code.
- **Nixodine:** a newer nicotine alternative used in some devices. See [what is Nixodine](/blog/what-is-nixodine/).
- **Nicotine pouch:** a small tobacco-free pouch placed between lip and gum. See [nicotine pouches beginner's guide](/blog/nicotine-pouches-beginners-guide/).

## Compliance terms
- **PACT Act:** a federal law covering remote sales of vapor products. See [the PACT Act explained](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/).
- **Adult signature:** delivery that requires a 21+ signature with ID. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/).
- **RMA:** a return authorization form used in our returns process.

## Abbreviations at a glance
MTL: mouth to lung. DTL: direct to lung. PG: propylene glycol. VG: vegetable glycerin. mAh: milliamp hours. W: watts. V: volts. Ω: ohms. USB-C: Universal Serial Bus type C. FDA: Food and Drug Administration. PACT: Prevent All Cigarette Trafficking.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Do I need to know all these terms?
No. Learn the few that matter for the device you are buying, and use the rest as a reference.

### Why are there so many words for the same thing?
The vaping community developed its own vocabulary over time, and different brands use different names. Where terms overlap, this guide notes it.

### Where do I find the strength on a product?
On the product page and the packaging, as mg/mL or a percentage. See [how to read a vape product page](/blog/how-to-read-a-vape-product-page/).

## Shop
Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Terms you will see on product pages, explained with examples
### "50K puffs, 5% nicotine, USB-C, mesh coil"
This tells you that the manufacturer estimates about 50,000 puffs, that the liquid contains 50 mg/mL of nicotine (5%), that the battery charges through a USB-C port and that the coil is made of mesh. Together, these describe a large, rechargeable disposable with a modern coil.

### "30 mL, 50/50, 35 mg salt"
This describes a 30-milliliter bottle of e-liquid with equal parts PG and VG and a nicotine-salt strength of 35 mg/mL. It suits a low-power pod.

### "100 mL shortfill, 70VG/30PG, 0 mg"
This is a 100-milliliter bottle with higher VG and no nicotine, usually sold with room to add nicotine shots in some markets. It suits a sub-ohm tank.

### "Kit, 1.2 ohm pod, 18 W, 1000 mAh"
This describes a starter kit with a 1.2 ohm pod, a power of 18 watts and a battery of 1,000 mAh. It suits mouth-to-lung inhaling.

## Words that mean different things in different places
Some terms are used loosely. "Mod" can mean any battery unit or a box device. "Atomizer" can mean the coil or the whole tank. "Cartridge" can mean a pre-filled pod or a replaceable coil head. "Juice" and "e-liquid" mean the same thing. If a term is unclear, check the product description, and ask us if you are unsure.

## Terms from the shop and the law
- **Age gate:** the confirmation that you are 21 or older when you enter a site.
- **Adult signature:** a delivery requirement. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/).
- **Warning statement:** the required nicotine warning. See [what the nicotine warning label means](/blog/what-the-nicotine-warning-label-means/).
- **Batch code:** a code printed on packaging that identifies a production run.
- **Counterfeit:** a fake product that imitates a brand. See [how to spot counterfeit vapes](/blog/how-to-spot-counterfeit-vapes/).

## Terms about use and care
- **Priming:** soaking a new coil before use.
- **Chain vaping:** taking puffs in quick succession, which can dry the wick.
- **Charge cycle:** one full discharge and recharge of a battery.
- **Pass-through:** using a device while it charges.
- **Leak:** liquid escaping from the tank or pod.

## Terms you can ignore for now
If you use a disposable, you can skip most electrical and coil terms. If you use a pod, learn pod, coil and strength. If you use a tank and mod, learn ohms, watts, airflow and PG/VG. Start with the words that match your device, and add more as you need them.

## Quick pronunciation and spelling notes
Ohm is written with the symbol Ω. Mod is short for modification. MTL and DTL are usually said as letters. Nic salts is pronounced as written. Sub-ohm is said "sub-ohm". These small points help when you read reviews and talk to other users.

## Tips for reading unfamiliar listings
Read the specifications first, because they are the least ambiguous part of a listing. Compare the same details across products, such as strength, volume, puffs and battery. Be cautious of listings that use many technical terms but give few concrete numbers. If you cannot tell what a product is, ask us before you buy.

## Terms about money and value
- **Cost per puff:** price divided by puffs, used to compare disposables. See [how to compare vape prices per puff](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/).
- **Cost per milliliter:** price divided by volume, used to compare bottles.
- **Bulk or wholesale:** buying larger quantities at lower unit prices. See [bulk buying tips](/blog/bulk-buying-vapes-save-money/).
- **Restocking fee:** a charge on some refunds that covers handling returned items.

## Terms about nicotine pouches
- **Pouch strength:** nicotine per pouch, in milligrams. See [nicotine pouch strengths explained](/blog/nicotine-pouch-strengths-explained/).
- **Slim, mini and regular:** pouch sizes.
- **Can:** the container, which usually holds around 15 to 20 pouches.

## Terms about devices you may meet less often
- **Rebuildable:** devices where you build your own coils. They need more skill.
- **Squonk mod:** a mod that feeds liquid from a bottle in the body. It is a niche device.
- **Pen style:** a slim device shaped like a pen.
- **Cartridge:** a pre-filled liquid container, used in some closed systems.

faq.a: Mouth to lung, an inhale style where you draw into your mouth first and then inhale, usually with a tight airflow and a higher-resistance coil.
A coil with resistance below one ohm, used with open airflow for direct-to-lung inhaling.
A smoother type of nicotine used in low-power devices such as pods and disposables.
A harsh, burnt draw caused by a dry wick.
Milliamp hours, a measure of battery capacity.
A lingering flavor from a previous liquid.
